description:
Data Standardizer provides implementations of various internationally recognised standards in data processing, covering topics ranging from languages to currencies and geographical entities. With strongly-typed enumerations for each standard (where applicable) or other targeted data types, you can represent these elements in your code such that errors with invalid values are minimised.

Provides types supporting the reading and writing of iCalendar files.  Includes:
- Internet Calendaring and Scheduling Core Object Specification (iCalendar), RFC 5545
- Parameter Value Encoding in iCalendar and vCard, RFC 6868
- New Properties for iCalendar, RFC 7986
- jCal: The JSON Format for iCalendar, RFC 7265
- xCal: The XML Format for iCalendar, RFC 6321
releaseNotes:
Breaking changes:
- A YEARLY rule with BYWEEKNO and no BYDAY occurs on the weekday of DTSTART, not every day of the week.
- `JcalReader` rejects a string where RFC 7265 requires a number, `true` or `false`, an array or an object, such as `"5"` for an INTEGER, a PERIOD joined by a solidus, a RECUR rule as text, or GEO items as strings.
- `JcalReader` and `IcalValue.TryParseInteger` with `IcalValueFormat.Json` no longer round a number that isn't whole, such as `1.0000000000000001`, to an integer.
- `JcalReader` rejects a RECUR rule part in a JSON form RFC 7265 doesn't allow, such as `"count": "2"`, `"until": 20260101` or `"freq": ["DAILY"]`.
- `IcalReader`, `IcalWriter`, `IcalValue.TryParseText` and `GetTextValue` reject an unescaped comma or semicolon in a TEXT value, such as `SUMMARY:Lunch, then review` (RFC 5545 section 3.3.11), and TEXT getters such as `IcalEvent.Summary` throw `IcalFileException` for one; the separators of CATEGORIES, RESOURCES, VERSION and REQUEST-STATUS are still allowed.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalWriter` report a REQUEST-STATUS value without a valid status code followed by `;` and a description, such as `REQUEST-STATUS:2.0`, as an invalid value (RFC 5545 section 3.8.8.3).
- The calendar readers and writers (`IcalReader`, `JcalReader`, `XcalReader` and their writers) report a DTEND or DUE that isn't later than DTSTART, or that is in local time when DTSTART isn't or the other way round, as an invalid value (RFC 5545 sections 3.8.2.2 and 3.8.2.3).
- The calendar readers and writers report a VFREEBUSY DTSTART or DTEND that isn't a DATE-TIME in UTC (RFC 5545 section 3.8.2.4), and a STATUS, TRANSP or CALSCALE value outside the set RFC 5545 defines, such as `STATUS:BANANA` or a VJOURNAL status on a VEVENT (sections 3.8.1.11, 3.8.2.7 and 3.7.1), as an invalid value.
- `IcalReader`, `JcalReader`, `XcalReader` and the writers reject a `VERSION` other than `2.0` or `2.0;2.0`, such as `VERSION:2` or `VERSION:1.0;2.0` (RFC 5545 §3.7.4).
- `IcalValue.TryFormatUri`, `TryFormatCalAddress` and the `Url`, `Organizer`, `Source` and `TimeZoneUrl` setters write a `Uri` as given (`OriginalString`), not as `AbsoluteUri`, and throw `ArgumentException` for text the readers reject (RFC 5545 §3.3.13), such as a space, a non-ASCII character or a Windows file path; percent-encode such characters, and give an internationalized host in ASCII, before creating the `Uri`.
- `XcalReader` rejects a DATE-TIME, TIME, DURATION or PERIOD value whose designators, such as `T`, `Z`, `P` or `H`, are lower case, which RFC 6321 doesn't allow. `IcalOptions.AllowInvalidValues` still accepts it.
- `IcalDateTime`, `IcalTime`, `IcalDuration` and `IcalPeriod` no longer parse lower-case designators in `IcalValueFormat.Xml` form. The `Text` and `Json` forms still accept them.
- `IcalAlarm.TriggerDateTime` throws `ArgumentException` when set to a floating date-time or one in a named time zone, instead of silently dropping the time zone. RFC 5545 §3.8.6.3 requires an absolute TRIGGER to be in UTC.
- `IcalReader`, `JcalReader` and `XcalReader` reject a calendar with no VERSION whatever the options; `AllowMissingRequiredProperties` no longer accepts it, and the `DiagnosticKind` is `UnsupportedVersion`.
- `IcalWriter`, `JcalWriter` and `XcalWriter` refuse a calendar with a property named BEGIN or END, which was written as the start or end of a component, and `JcalReader` and `XcalReader` reject one; the `DiagnosticKind` is `InvalidComponentNesting`.
- JcalReader and XcalReader reject a value written in the iCalendar text form instead of the jCal or xCal form.
- `XcalReader` rejects the child elements of a `recur`, `period`, `geo` or `request-status` element out of the order RFC 6321 Appendix A gives them, a repeated `freq`, `interval` or `wkst`, or both `until` and `count`, a `parameters` element after a property's value, and a `components` element before `properties`.
- `XcalReader` reports a lower-case `freq`, `wkst` or `byday` weekday as an invalid value, as RFC 6321 Appendix A (3.3.10) requires upper case.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalWriter` reject a `RECURRENCE-ID` whose value type differs from the `DTSTART` of the recurring component in the calendar, or that is in local time with no time zone when that `DTSTART` is not, or the other way round (RFC 5545 section 3.8.4.4); `IcalOptions.AllowInvalidValues` accepts it.
- `IcalComponent.Validate`, `IcalWriter`, `JcalWriter` and `XcalWriter` report a component object nested in more than one place as `InvalidComponentNesting`; give each place a component of its own.
- `DtStamp`, `Created`, `LastModified` and `IcalTodo.Completed` throw `ArgumentException` when set to a floating date-time or one in a named time zone, on every component that has them. RFC 5545 requires these properties to be in UTC; the value used to be stored and rejected only when the calendar was written.
- `XcalReader` and `JcalReader` reject a component, property, parameter or rule part name that isn't in lower case, and `JcalReader` a type identifier that isn't (RFC 6321 §3.3 to §3.5, RFC 7265 §3.3 to §3.6).
- `IcalFreeBusy.DtStart` and `DtEnd` throw `ArgumentException` when set to a DATE, a floating date-time or one in a named time zone. RFC 5545 requires them to be a DATE-TIME in UTC in a VFREEBUSY; the value used to be stored and rejected only when the calendar was written.
- `IcalTimeZoneObservance.DtStart` throws `ArgumentException` when set to a date-time in UTC or in a named time zone. RFC 5545 requires the start of a time zone observance to be a local date-time; the value used to be stored and rejected only when the calendar was written.
- `IcalTimeZoneObservance.RecurrenceRules` throws `ArgumentException` when a rule's `UNTIL` is a date or a local date-time. RFC 5545 requires the `UNTIL` of a time zone observance's rule to be in UTC; the rule used to be stored and rejected only when the calendar was written.
- A reader and a writer report the `UNTIL` of a recurrence rule in a STANDARD or DAYLIGHT observance as an invalid value when it isn't a date-time in UTC, also when the observance has no `DTSTART` or its `DTSTART` is a date. RFC 5545 §3.3.10 requires a UTC `UNTIL` there; such a calendar used to be read and written. `IcalOptions.AllowInvalidValues` accepts it.

Fixed:
- JCal and xCal writers keep the GEO and REQUEST-STATUS structure when VALUE names the default type.
- Recurrence rules are written with the FREQ rule part first, as RFC 5545 requires, including rules read from jCal, xCal or an .ics file with FREQ elsewhere.
- The xCal writer puts the rule parts of a recur element in the order RFC 6321 gives them, with FREQ, WKST and BYDAY weekdays in upper case.
- `IcalComponent.Validate`, `IcalWriter`, `JcalWriter` and `XcalWriter` report a component nested in itself, or nested more than 64 levels deep, as `InvalidComponentNesting` instead of ending the process with a stack overflow.
- FLOAT values are written with the same shortest digits on .NET Framework as on .NET 10, so a GEO coordinate no longer changes on write.
- `XcalWriter` writes the designators of a DURATION in upper case, as RFC 6321 requires, when it was read from `.ics` data in lower case.
- `XcalReader` keeps the parameters of each property when its `XmlReader` gives no line information, such as an `XmlNodeReader`.
- `IcalReader` and `IcalWriter` no longer reject a `RECURRENCE-ID` whose value type matches the `DTSTART` of the recurring component but not the instance's own `DTSTART`, such as a DATE for an all-day series whose instance moved to a time of day (RFC 5545 section 3.8.4.4).
- FLOAT values are read as the same double on .NET Framework as on .NET 10, including negative zero.
